newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-LEICESTER DESTROY TOULOUSE TO REACH FINAL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LEICESTER DESTROY TOULOUSE TO REACH FINAL.

text.p: Leicester produced one of the great performances of their distinguished history to reach the European Cup final by demolishing holders Toulouse 37-11 on Saturday.
The French triple champions again showed their dislike at playing in England as they displayed little skill or spirit in managing only one try to Leicester's five.
After their thrashing by Wasps in the pool matches Touslouse have now conceded 114 points in two cross-channel fixtures in this tournament and exit with their reputation in tatters.

Leicester cashed in on frequent blunders by Toulouse and created their own chances through their powerful forwards and gifted backs. Their opponents in the final later this month will be either Brive or Cardiff who meet in the other semifinal in France on Sunday.

Toulouse lost their discipline and tempers and conceded a steady run of penalties in the second half. Christophe Deylaud conceded three dissent penalties inside 10 seconds and when hooker Patrick Soula was substituted he made an obscene gesture towards the crowd.
Toulouse managed only two first half penalties through fly-half Christophe Deylaud and nothing more until a try of small consolation by wing Michel Marfaing in the dying moments.
Leicester dominated throughout, always using the option of spinning the ball wide or using it cleverly down the blindside.
Lock Martin Johnson delivered a steady supply of ball from the lineouts and in the backs Austin Healey, Rob Liley and Will Greenwood all pressured the French defence.
Leicester were put on their way when winger Steve Hackney intercepted an appalling pass by Toulouse centre Thomas Castaignede to sprint 60 yards unopposed for a try.
Stuart Potter and Greenwood cashed in on another French mistake to put flanker Neil Back in for another comfortable try. Full-back John Liley converted both.
Deylaud and Liley exchanged a couple of penalties each in the second quarter, enabling Leicester to retain their 14-point advantage and the Tigers struck crucially in the 48th minute.
Leicester's classic rolling maul gave prop Darren Garforth a free ball and open space on the blindside for a try for 25-6 from which there was no comeback.
In the 66th minute Leicester were easily achieving a push-over try when referee Jim Fleming punished Toulouse for illegally preventing it and awarded a penalty try.
Leicester signed off with the sort of try that might have been created by a flowing French team, with Liley making progress before Greenwood caught his own kick before sending Healey in.
